note.explanation: A physical quantity can be measured with tools or instruments. A non-physical quantity cannot be measured with tools and instruments; it may be described or compared using agreed criteria or surveys.
examples: Length is a physical quantity because it can be measured with a ruler.
Fear is a non-physical quantity because it cannot be measured with a measuring instrument.
note.checkAnswer: No. A non-physical quantity cannot be measured with tools and instruments, so it has no measurable magnitude and unit.
note.simple: If you can measure it with an instrument and give its result as a number with a unit, it is a physical quantity. If you cannot, it is non-physical.
note.checkQuestion: Does a non-physical quantity have dimensions?
note.title: Physical and Non-Physical Quantities
steps: Ask whether the quantity can be measured with a tool or instrument.
If it can be measured, classify it as a physical quantity.
If it cannot be measured, classify it as a non-physical quantity.
For a physical measurement, state its numerical value and unit.
note.answer: A physical quantity can be measured; a non-physical quantity cannot be measured with tools and instruments.

mcqs.stem: Which of the following is a physical quantity?
rationales: Length can be measured using an instrument, so it is physical.
Beauty cannot be measured with a measuring instrument, so it is non-physical.
Wisdom cannot be measured with a measuring instrument, so it is non-physical.
Affection cannot be measured with a measuring instrument, so it is non-physical.

mcqs.stem: Which quantity can be measured using a suitable instrument?
rationales: Fear is non-physical and cannot be measured with an instrument.
Temperature can be measured using a thermometer, so it is physical.
Love is non-physical and cannot be measured with an instrument.
Beauty is non-physical and cannot be measured with an instrument.

mcqs.stem: Which is a way to compare or describe a non-physical quantity?
rationales: A ruler measures length, which is a physical quantity.
A clock measures time, which is a physical quantity.
A thermometer measures temperature, which is a physical quantity.
A survey can be used to compare or describe non-physical quantities.

mcqs.stem: Which quantity can be measured directly or indirectly using tools and instruments?
rationales: Fear cannot be measured using tools and instruments.
Volume can be measured, so it is a physical quantity.
Wisdom cannot be measured using tools and instruments.
Affection cannot be measured using tools and instruments.

mcqs.stem: Which example is a physical quantity?
rationales: The length of an object can be measured with a ruler.
Beauty is a non-physical quantity and cannot be measured with an instrument.
Love is a non-physical quantity and cannot be measured with an instrument.
Fear is a non-physical quantity and cannot be measured with an instrument.

options: A physical quantity can be measured.
A non-physical quantity must be measured with a ruler.
A physical quantity is only a feeling.
A non-physical quantity always has a measuring instrument.
mcqs.stem: Which statement best describes a physical quantity?
rationales: A physical quantity is measurable using tools or instruments.
A non-physical quantity cannot be measured with a ruler or other measuring instrument.
Feelings such as fear and affection are non-physical quantities.
Non-physical quantities cannot be measured with instruments.

written.text: Can a non-physical quantity be measured? If yes, then how?
written.finalAnswer: No, not with tools and instruments; it can be described qualitatively or compared using pre-determined criteria, indices or surveys.

example.question: Use the textbook's examples to identify three physical quantities and the instruments used to measure them.
example.answer: Length—ruler; time duration—clock; temperature—thermometer. All are physical quantities.

explain.title: Physical quantities
explain.body: “Some of these can be measured directly and indirectly using some tools and instruments such as length of an object using a ruler, time duration of an event using a clock, the temperature (the degree of hotness) of somebody using a thermometer. They are called physical quantities.” A physical quantity can be measured, and physics uses physical quantities to express its laws and principles.

explain.title: Non-physical quantities
explain.body: “Other quantities quoted above such as love, affection, fear, wisdom, and beauty cannot be measured using tools and instruments.” These are non-physical quantities. They may be described qualitatively or compared using criteria, indices or surveys.

explain.title: Compare the two types
explain.body: Physical quantities can be measured and have a numerical value and a unit. Non-physical quantities cannot be measured with instruments. For example, length is physical, while fear is non-physical.

mistakes: Do not call something physical just because it can be described in words; it must be measurable with tools or instruments.
Do not confuse a survey or agreed criterion with direct measurement by a physical instrument.
When giving examples, use measurable quantities such as length, volume, density, time or temperature for physical quantities.
Do not claim that a non-physical quantity has a measurement unit or instrument.
